BVR practice 4v5 · 22:39Z

Virtual Egyptian Air Force · 2026-11-26 · AI-assisted debrief · approved by Sword
TRAININGA-ABVR

Instructor narrative

EAF Caucasus Training sortie 48905 ran 15 discrete BVR/A-A rounds over approximately 75 minutes, generating one of the highest-volume PVP datasets in recent squadron history. Blue won 9 of 15 rounds and red 4, with 2 withdrawals, giving blue a marginal overall edge but no dominant performance. Wade led all pilots with 15 tracker-confirmed kills, though his over-G pattern — 8 sustained exceedances in one slot alone and 40+ across the sortie — represents a structural airmanship failure that must be addressed before he is cleared for high-stress BVR tasking. [EAF] 9g | Sword debuted in a full BVR role in Rounds 12–15 and produced the most efficient kill-to-shot ratio in the session, though catastrophic formation-join times (worst 357 s) mean his tactical geometry was consistently degraded when he arrived. Maverick continues a declining trend with peak G-loads of 11.6–11.9 g on multiple occasions — the highest recorded — and long-range shot indiscipline burning missiles at 36–43 nm for zero kills. Omar showed the most tactical consistency of the red-side pilots, with an intelligent first-shot kill at 11.4 nm in Round 1 and a credible double-kill in Round 13, but his death rate remains too high to generate the net positive contribution his kill count suggests. PushMaster's 7 kills were offset by double-digit deaths and persistent long-range shot selection; his brief F-15E integration in Rounds 13–15 produced negligible effect until slot 14. Borhms was the most tactically versatile red-side pilot — mixing AIM-120 and AIM-9 in Round 7, achieving the highest crank time (97 s) in the session, and defeating 3 of 3 inbound missiles in Round 8 — but was hampered by a 284-second join time in Round 15 and a wasted slot in the red F-16 role. Cyclone accumulated the most flight time but generated only 2 kills from 68 minutes airborne, spraying missiles at 32–62 nm with CPAs up to 40 km — the shots fired simply do not match any viable parameters. Hema's late entry in Round 12 showed genuine promise with an efficient first-shot kill and a Round 15 double-kill, but Round 13's three consecutive extreme-range misses (22–35 km CPAs) indicate inconsistency. Server lag of up to 30 s was recorded in multiple slots and has been discounted for timing-sensitive assessments; kill/death attributions are based solely on tracker killDetails, not the DCS event dump.
  • Shot discipline defines the BVR fight: the majority of wasted missiles in this sortie were fired at 30–43 nm — beyond the 25 nm zero-credit band — where Pk approaches zero against a defending opponent. Pilots must internalize the shot band: full Pk inside 15 nm, half credit 15–25 nm, zero beyond. If you cannot sort a target inside 25 nm, do not shoot.
  • Over-G is a safety issue, not a performance metric: multiple pilots (Maverick 11.9 g, Hema 11.9 g, Borhms 11.5 g, Wade 10.3 g) exceeded the F-16/F-18 9-g structural limit on multiple occasions. In a real aircraft these would trigger mandatory inspections or fleet-wide groundings. G awareness drills and corner speed management must be incorporated into the next sortie's pre-brief.
  • Formation join time matters for BVR geometry: Sword's 357-second worst join and Borhms's 284-second join in Round 15 mean both pilots were out of their azimuth spread positions for most of those rounds, handing the merge entirely to solo opponents. Target: rejoin to within 30 seconds; if that cannot be achieved, a tactical reform must be called on frequency.

Pilot evaluations

C

Pushmaster

55 pts
participation_base 10 · flight_time_credit 5 · aa_kills_scored 20 · shot_discipline_penalty -15 · over_g_penalty -10 · defense_credit 5 · survival_credit 2 · round_win_contribution 4 · airmanship_deduction -6
+ Round 4 slot 3: 100% Pk — 1 shot (34.7 nm AIM-120C), 1 splash on Maverick (CPA 147 m, TOF 48 s) — showed PushMaster can generate a quality shot when patient.
+ Round 8 slot 8: best defensive performance — 5 of 6 inbound missiles defeated (avgDefeatCPA 14,534 m), survived the round without being killed while generating 2 splashes.
− Long-range shot indiscipline dominated: multiple shots at 30–37 nm (outside the full-credit band), including 34.7 nm in Round 4, 30.1 nm in Round 5, 37.5 nm in Round 7 — PushMaster must learn to hold fire until inside 25 nm.
− Death rate remains high — killed in 10+ individual slots; several of these followed shots that failed to find target, leaving PushMaster defensive and out of energy.
Airmanship: PushMaster's trend (94→74 historically) shows meaningful regression, and this sortie's 55 score continues the decline. The switch to F-15E in rounds 13–15 saw no shots fired in the first two slots before finally generating a kill in slot 14 on Maverick. Over-G is present (5 exceedances in slot 8, 3 in slot 10) but less extreme than Maverick. The primary issue is shot selection — waiting for shots inside 20 nm would dramatically improve Pk. Cranking and notching mechanics were visible in some slots (crank time 105 s in slot 10 round 11) showing awareness but not yet execution.
C

Omar

59 pts
participation_base 10 · flight_time_credit 5 · aa_kills_scored 20 · shot_discipline_penalty -8 · over_g_penalty -14 · defense_credit 8 · survival_credit 2 · round_win_contribution 6 · airmanship_deduction -10
+ Round 2 slot 1: perfect first-shot kill at 11.4 nm on Wade (CPA 180 m), demonstrated correct shot timing — patience rewarded with a clean splash from inside the 15 nm band.
+ Round 13 slot 11: 2 kills from 3 shots — splashes on Cyclone (11.1 nm, CPA 172 m) and again via proximity (35 nm TARGET_DOWN_MIDFLIGHT), plus a 3rd splash on Sword at 7.3 nm (CPA 10 m) — Omar's best round of the session.
− 6 sustained over-G exceedances in slots 10 and 11 (maxG 9.47 g in slot 11, 9.23 g in slot 10) — Omar consistently pulls sustained high-G without deliberate technique; needs to manage G onset and check G meter during turns.
− Death rate is high relative to kills — multiple rounds where Omar was killed having fired 0 shots (Round 6 slot: 0 shots, 1 death; Round 15 slot 13: same pattern), suggesting poor energy and positional awareness when the merge goes adverse.
Airmanship: Omar shows flashes of genuine BVR instinct (the 11.4 nm kill in Round 1 was textbook, and the Round 13 double-kill was effective) but the over-G flag appears repeatedly throughout the session. The trend from history (44→70) is positive and this sortie supports continued improvement, but the high death-to-kill ratio (approximately 1:1 overall) limits the score. minAGL was 55 ft in one slot — extremely low for a BVR profile.

Wade

72 pts
“15 kills and the best combat record in the session, but 40+ over-G exceedances across the sortie make him an airframe-wrecker who cannot be cleared for ops until G discipline is enforced.”
participation_base 10 · flight_time_credit 5 · aa_kills_scored 30 · shot_discipline_penalty -12 · over_g_penalty -15 · defense_credit 8 · survival_credit 6 · round_win_contribution 10 · airmanship_deduction -10
+ Tracker-confirmed 15 air kills across 15 rounds — highest raw kill count in the session, including multiple 2-kill frames (Rounds 6, 8, 10, 11, 14) and a clean 100% Pk double in Round 10 (shots at 34.3 nm and 32.6 nm both splashed, CPA 2 m and 107 m).
+ Round 8 was textbook: two kills from 35.7 nm and 34.5 nm without a single inbound missile — zero shots received, 100% survive.
− Over-G is a career-threatening pattern: 8 sustained exceedances flagged in a single 4.6-minute slot (Round 11 slot 9), and totals across all slots run to 40+ individual flagged exceedances — this is structural, not incidental; airframe stress management must be addressed immediately.
− Long-range shot discipline is poor — multiple shots at 38–40 nm (beyond the 25 nm zero-credit band) including a 39.9 nm shot in Round 1 and a 40 nm shot in Round 2 that wasted missiles; average launch range in some slots exceeded 24 nm with low Pk.
Airmanship: Consistently fast and aggressive — avg speeds 820–989 kt across slots, minAGL as low as 19 ft (Aerial-2-10 slot). Notch quality was present in later rounds (Round 10 spent 73 s notching). Formation data sparse but Wade operated largely solo or as a singleton shooter. The over-G count is the dominant airmanship issue — if this were a live frame, structural inspection would be mandatory.

The 0-shot/killed slot in the red F-16 role in Round 15 is the main airmanship flag — adaptability to tasked role is a professional requirement.

+ Round 6 slot 1: shot-for-shot efficiency — 1 round fired, 1 splash, 100% Pk on PushMaster at 27 nm (CPA 313 m) showing Maverick can generate a quality shot under pressure.

Formation discipline showed some improvement in later rounds (best join 10 s in slot 9) but score of 1.8 in Round 12 slot 7 and 0 in multiple other slots demonstrates this is not yet consistent. Shot selection at extreme range remains the tactical deficiency.
